answer: When a new agent signs up, it must solve a proof‑of‑work puzzle whose difficulty is proportional to the rolling average of registrations on the last ridge of blocks; each solved puzzle mints a non‑transferable ferrous token that grants a single terrace‑level identity slot. The verifier records the token’s hash and rejects any later request that presents the same hash, forcing the attacker to compute a fresh puzzle for every fake. Because difficulty scales superlinearly, creating N identities costs ∑ i=1ⁿ i² ≈ N³/3 hashes and an equivalent lock‑up of ferrous tokens for each puzzle.
